note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is "customised" guest service?
options: Giving every guest exactly the same service, in the same way
Offering only the services that are listed in the brochure
Letting guests do all the work themselves to save on staff
Shaping the service to each guest's own needs and likes

questions.stem: Why do villas offer customised service?
options: So that they can charge every guest more for the room
So guests feel valued, enjoy the stay and come back
So that staff can skip the standard cleaning tasks
So that guests stay inside the villa the whole time

questions.stem: When is the best time to find out a villa guest's likes and needs?
options: Before arrival, with a pre-arrival form or call
On the last day, when the guest is checking out
Only if the guest complains during the stay
After the guest has gone home, by letter

questions.stem: Which question belongs on a pre-arrival preference form?
options: How much money do you earn each year?
Which political party do you support?
Do you have any food allergies or dietary needs?
How many times have you been married?

questions.stem: What is a "guest history" or guest profile?
options: A list of the guest's past complaints, to warn other staff
The guest's bank details, kept for the next booking
A record of a guest's past stays and preferences
A diary that staff keep of what the guest does each day

questions.stem: Who may see a guest's profile?
options: Only staff who need it to serve the guest
Any guest who asks about another guest
Friends of staff who visit the villa
Anyone, as it is kept on a shared page online

questions.stem: A repeat guest likes a firm pillow and a cool room. When should you set these up?
options: When the guest asks again after arriving
On the second day of the stay
Only if the guest has time to remind you
Before the guest arrives at the villa

questions.stem: A guest's pre-arrival form asks for the fridge to be stocked. What do you need to agree with them?
options: Nothing; buy whatever the shop has most of
A shopping list, a budget and how they will pay
Only the time that the guest's flight lands
The name of the guest's favourite shop at home

questions.stem: You buy groceries for a guest. What should you give them with the items?
options: Nothing, as it was a small amount of money
The receipt and any change, counted out
A note of the price you think it cost
Only the change, as the receipt is for the shop

questions.stem: How should you greet a returning guest whose name you know?
options: With a quick wave, so that you do not disturb them
By asking for their name again, in case it changed
By calling them by their first name and a nickname
Warmly, using their title and surname, with a welcome back

questions.stem: The booking says a couple are celebrating their 25th wedding anniversary. What could you arrange, if the villa allows it?
options: A card and a small cake or flowers in the room on arrival
A loud party with other guests they do not know
Nothing, as it is a private matter for the couple
A bill for a celebration they did not ask for

questions.stem: A guest asks you to keep her husband's birthday surprise a secret. What should you do?
options: Tell the husband so that he can plan his outfit
Tell the other staff to mention it to him at breakfast
Keep it a secret and help her to plan the surprise
Refuse, as surprises are against the villa's rules

questions.stem: A guest is allergic to peanuts. What must you do?
options: Tell the cook to use only a little peanut in each dish
Remove the peanuts from the top of the dish before serving
Leave it to the guest to check every meal themselves
Record it, tell the cook and check every dish and snack

questions.stem: A guest is vegetarian. Which dish is suitable?
options: Ackee and callaloo with fried dumplings
Curry goat with white rice and salad
Jerk chicken with festival and slaw
Escovitch fish with bammy and salad

questions.stem: A guest tells you they eat only halal food. What does this mean for the meals?
options: They eat no fruit or vegetables at all
No pork or alcohol, and only halal meat
They eat only food that is served raw
They want very spicy food at every meal

questions.stem: A guest who uses a wheelchair is arriving. What should you check in the villa?
options: That the rugs are thick and the furniture close together
That the room is upstairs, for the best view of the sea
That the route to the room and bathroom has no steps
That the bathroom has a deep bathtub instead of a shower

questions.stem: How should you speak to a guest who is hard of hearing?
options: Face them, speak clearly and offer to write things down
Shout loudly from across the room so that they can hear
Speak only to the person who is with them instead
Speak very fast so that the talk is over quickly

questions.stem: A family with a toddler is arriving. What might you prepare, if they asked for it?
options: A glass table and sharp ornaments at the child's height
A pool gate left open so the child can play near the water
Strong cleaning products in a low, open cupboard
A baby cot, a high chair and covers for the plug sockets

questions.stem: An older guest finds the stairs hard. What is a helpful step?
options: Tell them to take the stairs slowly each time
Give them the room at the top of the villa
Offer them a room on the ground floor, if one is free
Remove the handrail so the stairs look nicer

questions.stem: A guest asks you to unpack their suitcase. What should you do?
options: Unpack it while they are out, without asking how they like it
Ask how they like things put away, and handle items with care
Leave the clothes on the bed so the guest can put them away
Look through their bag pockets and read any papers inside

questions.stem: While unpacking, you find a guest's jewellery. What should you do?
options: Ask where they want it, or suggest the safe
Try it on to see if it fits, then put it back
Put it in your pocket and give it back later
Leave it out on the dressing table by the window

questions.stem: A guest asks you to press a silk shirt. What should you check first?
options: That the iron is on its hottest setting
That the shirt is still damp from the pool
The care label, for the right iron setting
That the shirt has been folded into a square

questions.stem: Guests want a private dinner on the beach. What must you check before setting it up?
options: That the table is set up below the high-tide line
That the candles are placed under the palm leaves
That other guests are invited to join them too
The weather, the tide and safe lighting

questions.stem: A guest wants a massage in the villa. What should you do?
options: Ask a staff member with no training to give the massage
Book a licensed therapist from the approved list
Tell them that massages are only for hotel guests
Give them a bottle of oil and let them do it themselves

questions.stem: What does it mean to "anticipate" a guest's needs?
options: To wait until the guest asks for something twice
To guess what the guest earns from their clothes
To notice and meet a need before the guest asks
To tell the guest what they must want to do

questions.stem: A guest comes back from a long walk in the sun. Which action shows you are anticipating their needs?
options: Offering a cold drink and a cool, damp face towel
Asking whether they can pay their bill now
Telling them about tomorrow's weather forecast
Asking them to remove their shoes at the door

questions.stem: A guest from another country has customs you do not know. What is the best approach?
options: Ask them to follow Jamaican customs while they stay
Respect them, and ask politely whenever you are unsure
Joke about the customs to make them feel relaxed
Avoid the guest so that you do not make a mistake

questions.stem: Guests are relaxing on the villa patio and talking privately. How should you serve them?
options: Join in the talk so that they feel welcome
Stand close by so you hear what they need
Interrupt to tell them about the staff's day
Serve quietly and step away until called

questions.stem: A famous guest is staying. A reporter phones to ask if they are there. What do you say?
options: Yes, and give the dates of the stay
Yes, but only say the room or villa name
Give the guest's phone number to the reporter
You cannot say who is staying here

questions.stem: A guest asks for a type of tea the local shops do not have. What should you do?
options: Say nothing and hope that they forget about it
Tell them it is their fault for asking for it
Explain kindly and offer a similar local choice
Buy a different tea and say it is the same one

questions.stem: A guest asks for something against the villa's rules, such as a party for 50 people. What should you do?
options: Explain the rule politely and offer what is allowed
Agree to it, and hope that the manager does not find out
Laugh and tell the guest that the idea is silly
Ignore the request and walk away from the guest

questions.stem: How can you check that a guest is happy with a special service?
options: Wait to read the review after they go home
Ask them politely and watch how they react
Ask the other staff what they think of it
Assume they are happy if they say nothing

questions.stem: A guest tells you they love fresh mango juice at breakfast. What should you do with this?
options: Remember it yourself and tell no one else
Record it in the guest profile for the team
Write it on a scrap of paper in your pocket
Tell the guest it is too costly to offer

questions.stem: Why should you pass on a guest's preferences at the staff briefing?
options: So that other staff can gossip about the guest
So that the guest can be charged for each one
So that only one staff member serves the guest
So every staff member gives the same personal service

questions.stem: A pre-arrival email asks the guest about "pillow preferences". What is this for?
options: To sell the guest a new pillow to take back home
To check the guest's height and weight
To have the right pillows ready in the room
To see whether the guest sleeps very late

questions.stem: A guest asks for "the usual" when they arrive. You do not know what it is. What should you do?
options: Check the profile, or ask kindly to be reminded
Guess, and bring the first drink you can find
Tell them there is no such thing as "the usual"
Ask another guest what this guest usually has

questions.stem: Which welcome is the most personal for a repeat guest who loves Blue Mountain coffee?
options: A printed card that says "Dear Guest"
The standard fruit bowl that every guest gets
A note by name with Blue Mountain coffee
A list of the villa's rules on the bedside table

questions.stem: A guest invites you to join them for drinks while you are on duty. What should you do?
options: Thank them politely and say you must stay on duty
Join them and drink, because the guest is always right
Tell them it is rude to ask staff to have a drink
Agree, then leave your work to the other staff

questions.stem: A guest asks for a beach set-up each morning. What does this usually include?
options: A tent, a camp stove and a fire on the sand
Loungers, towels, an umbrella and cold water
The villa's indoor dining table and its chairs
A loud music system and a bar

questions.stem: A guest emails a long list of requests before arrival. What should you do first?
options: Do the easy ones and ignore the rest
Wait until the guests arrive before reading it
Forward it to the guest's travel agent
Reply to confirm what can be done, and when

questions.stem: A guest's special request was forgotten, and the guest is upset. What should you do?
options: Say sorry, fix it fast and tell your supervisor
Blame the staff member who was on duty yesterday
Tell the guest that the request was never made
Offer a free night at once without asking anyone

questions.stem: A guest speaks little English. How can you help them?
options: Speak louder and faster until they understand
Use simple words, gestures or a translation app
Avoid speaking to them unless they speak first
Ask them to bring a friend every time they need help

questions.stem: Housekeeping notices that a guest always moves the desk chair out to the balcony. What is a customised response?
options: Move it back to the desk every day
Tell the guest that furniture must not be moved
Leave it there, or offer a balcony chair
Remove the chair from the room for good

questions.stem: A guest asks for a private chef dinner, which has an extra charge. What must you do before booking it?
options: Book it and add the charge to the bill later
Tell the guest it is free, to keep them happy
Ask the chef to choose a price after the meal
Tell the guest the full cost and get their OK

questions.stem: At the end of the stay, why do you ask the guest to fill in a feedback form?
options: To check that they have paid all the tips
To find out where they will go on their next holiday
To learn what they liked and what to improve
To ask them to book again at a lower price

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A door sign says "DND". What do the letters DND stand for?
What is the hospitality word for a small welcome gift, such as fruit or a card, placed in a guest's room?
What is the name of a severe, life-threatening allergic reaction that needs emergency help at once?
What is the name of a diet with no animal products at all: no meat, fish, eggs, milk or honey?
"Kosher" food follows the food rules of which religion?
What one word means keeping quiet about guests' private matters and serving them without drawing attention?
At a luxury villa, what is the job title of the staff member who looks after guests' personal needs, such as unpacking and serving drinks?
What is the name for a sloping path used instead of steps by guests in wheelchairs?
Which Jamaican drink, made from a deep red flower, is a favourite at Christmas time?
What is the name of the evening service in which the bed is folded back, the lights dimmed and the curtains drawn?
What word is used for a guest's likes and wishes, such as a firm pillow or a cool room, that are kept in their profile?
What is the name for suggesting a better or extra service to a guest, such as a sunset cruise, when it suits them?
Which dark, spiced Jamaican loaf is often eaten with cheese at Easter?
What is the name for a food or ingredient, such as nuts or shellfish, that can cause an allergic reaction?
What is the name for a basket of food and drink that staff pack for guests to take to the beach or a waterfall?

essays.stem: Explain how you would find out a guest's preferences before they arrive and during their stay.
essays.modelAnswer: Before arrival, I would check the guest profile for any past stays and read the booking notes. I would then send a friendly pre-arrival form or make a call, asking about the arrival time, the number of guests and their ages, food allergies and dietary needs, pillow and room temperature preferences, any special occasions, and what they would like stocked in the fridge or arranged, such as tours, a chef or airport transfers. I would confirm in writing what can be done. During the stay, I would listen to what guests say and watch what they do: for example, if a guest always takes coffee black or moves a chair to the balcony. I would ask politely whether everything is as they like it. I would record every preference in the guest profile and share it with the team.
markingPoints: Checks the guest profile and booking notes first
Pre-arrival form or call covering arrival, guests, diet and allergies, room likes, occasions, services
Confirms in writing what can be done
During the stay, listens, watches and asks politely
Records preferences in the profile and shares them with the team

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare a villa for a returning guest whose profile lists their preferences.
essays.modelAnswer: I would read the guest's profile and the new booking carefully, and note anything that has changed, such as a new family member. At the staff briefing I would share the preferences with the team. Before arrival, I would set up the bedroom with the pillows they like, set the air conditioning to the temperature they prefer, and put out their favourite toiletries or extra towels. I would stock the fridge and pantry with their usual items, such as fresh fruit, juice and Blue Mountain coffee, keeping the receipts. I would tell the cook about any allergies or dislikes. I would place a personal welcome note, signed by the team, with a small local amenity. Finally, I would check the whole villa against a checklist so that nothing is missed, and be ready to greet them warmly by name.
markingPoints: Reads the profile and booking and notes any changes
Shares the preferences with the team
Sets up the room to the preferences (pillows, temperature, toiletries)
Stocks the fridge and tells the cook about allergies and dislikes
Personal welcome note and amenity; final check; greets by name

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and set up a surprise anniversary dinner for a couple staying at a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: First, I would agree the plan with the guest who asked for it: the date and time, where they want it (on the patio or the beach), the budget, the menu and any allergies, and whether the surprise must be kept secret. I would tell the guest the full cost and get their agreement. I would check the weather and have an indoor plan in case of rain. I would agree the menu with the cook, perhaps with Jamaican dishes such as grilled lobster or jerk chicken and a rum cake for dessert. I would order flowers and a card. On the day, I would set a table for two with a clean cloth, napkins, glassware and safe lighting, such as candles in glass holders, away from anything that can burn. I would serve quietly, give the couple privacy, and afterwards ask the guest how it went.
markingPoints: Agrees details with the guest: date, place, budget, menu, allergies, secrecy
Gives the full cost and gets agreement
Checks weather and has an indoor plan
Arranges the menu, flowers and card; sets the table neatly and safely
Serves discreetly and follows up afterwards

essays.stem: Explain how to deal safely with a guest's food allergy, from the booking to serving the meal.
essays.modelAnswer: When the booking is made or on the pre-arrival form, I would ask about allergies and record them clearly in the guest profile, for example "severe peanut allergy". I would tell the cook and every staff member who serves food, at the briefing and in writing. When shopping, I would read every label to check for the allergen, and keep allergen-free food apart. The cook should use clean boards, pans and utensils so that there is no cross-contact. Before serving, I would check each dish and snack with the cook, and tell the guest what is in it if they ask. If I am not sure what is in something, I would not serve it. Staff should know the signs of a serious reaction, such as swelling or trouble breathing, and call an ambulance at once. I would never guess or say a dish is safe when I am not sure.
markingPoints: Asks about and records allergies clearly
Tells the cook and all serving staff
Reads labels when shopping and prevents cross-contact (clean boards and utensils)
Checks every dish before serving; does not serve if unsure
Knows the signs of a serious reaction and calls an ambulance at once

essays.stem: Describe how you would make a villa stay comfortable and safe for a guest who uses a wheelchair, or an older guest who walks slowly.
essays.modelAnswer: Before arrival, I would ask the guest politely what help they need, rather than guessing. I would give them a room on the ground floor, if possible, with a step-free route from the car to the room, bathroom, dining area and pool deck. I would move furniture to leave wide, clear paths, take up loose rugs and remove trip hazards. In the bathroom, I would check that grab rails and a shower seat are in place if the villa has them, and put a non-slip mat in the shower. Things the guest uses often, such as the phone, lights and water, would be within easy reach. I would offer help with luggage and doors, but let the guest decide. I would speak to the guest directly, not only to their companion. I would record their needs in the profile for the next stay.
markingPoints: Asks the guest what help they need
Ground-floor room and step-free route
Clear wide paths; loose rugs and trip hazards removed
Bathroom safety (grab rails, shower seat, non-slip mat) and items within reach
Offers help respectfully, speaks to the guest directly and records the needs

essays.stem: Describe how you would give a guest an unpacking service, and then a packing service at the end of the stay.
essays.modelAnswer: I would only unpack when the guest asks, and I would ask how they like things put away. I would work with clean hands, place the suitcase on the luggage rack, not the bed, and handle each item with care. Shirts, dresses and jackets go on hangers; folded items go in the drawers by type; shoes go on the floor of the wardrobe; and toiletries go neatly in the bathroom. I would not open private papers, wallets or medicines, and I would ask where the guest wants jewellery and valuables, suggesting the room safe. When packing, I would check every drawer, the wardrobe, the safe and the bathroom so that nothing is left behind. I would fold clothes with tissue paper, put shoes in bags, place heavy items at the bottom, and keep liquids sealed in a plastic bag. I would ask the guest to check before closing.
markingPoints: Asks first and finds out how the guest likes things
Handles items with care; case on the rack; hangs and folds correctly
Respects privacy: no private papers; valuables to the safe as the guest wishes
Packing: checks all drawers, wardrobe, safe and bathroom
Packs neatly (heavy items at the bottom, shoes bagged, liquids sealed) and lets the guest check

essays.stem: Explain why privacy and discretion matter when giving personal service to villa guests. Give examples.
essays.modelAnswer: Villa guests often choose a villa because they want privacy. Staff see and hear a lot of private things, so guests must be able to trust them. If staff gossip or share details, guests may feel unsafe, complain or never return, and the villa's name is harmed. Some guests may also be famous, or have health or family matters they want kept quiet. Examples of discretion: never telling anyone, including callers or reporters, who is staying; knocking and waiting before entering a room; respecting the Do Not Disturb sign; serving quietly and stepping away when guests are talking; not reading papers or looking through bags when tidying; keeping guest profiles locked or password protected; and never posting photos of guests or their things on social media. Discreet staff make guests feel relaxed and at home.
markingPoints: Guests choose villas for privacy and must be able to trust staff
Gossip or sharing details harms trust, causes complaints and harms the villa
Never confirms who is staying to callers or reporters
Knocks, respects DND, serves quietly, does not look at private items
Keeps profiles secure and never posts guests on social media

essays.stem: Explain how you should respond when a guest asks for something you cannot provide.
essays.modelAnswer: First, I would listen carefully to the request and make sure I understand exactly what the guest wants and why. I would check with my supervisor or the approved supplier list, in case there is a way to do it. If it really cannot be done, for example because a product is not sold in Jamaica, it breaks the villa's rules, or it is not safe, I would explain this politely and honestly, without blaming the guest or making excuses. I would then offer the closest choice that is possible, such as a similar local product, another time or a different service, and let the guest decide. I would never promise what I cannot deliver. I would record the request and what was agreed, follow up later to check that the guest is happy, and tell the manager, as many guests may want the same thing in future.
markingPoints: Listens and checks exactly what is wanted
Checks with the supervisor or suppliers before saying no
Explains politely and honestly why it cannot be done
Offers the closest alternative and lets the guest choose; never promises what cannot be done
Records it, follows up and tells the manager

essays.stem: Describe how a villa can give a customised stay to a family with young children.
essays.modelAnswer: Before arrival, I would ask the parents the children's ages and what they need, such as a baby cot, a high chair, a stair gate or a step for the bathroom sink. I would make the villa safe: plug socket covers, cleaning products and medicines locked away, sharp or glass ornaments moved up high, and the pool gate kept closed and locked. I would tell the parents that children must be watched by an adult near the pool at all times. I would stock the fridge with child-friendly food and drinks the parents choose, such as local fruit, juice and milk, and ask about any allergies. I could offer children's towels, toys or games, and suggest family-friendly tours. If the parents want a night out, I would arrange a checked babysitter from the approved list. I would record what worked well in the family's profile.
markingPoints: Asks the ages and needs before arrival (cot, high chair, stair gate)
Child-safe villa: socket covers, chemicals locked away, breakables moved, pool gate locked
Reminds parents to supervise children near the pool
Child-friendly food after asking about allergies; toys or family activities
Checked babysitter from the approved list; records in the profile

essays.stem: Explain how guest preferences should be recorded and shared with the team, and why this helps the villa win repeat business.
essays.modelAnswer: Each preference should be written in the guest profile as soon as it is known, clearly and in plain words, with the date, for example "Mrs Grant: firm pillows, room at 23 degrees, no shellfish, loves mango juice at breakfast". The profile is kept in the villa's system or a locked file, and only staff who need it can see it. Before and during each stay, the supervisor shares the key points at the staff briefing, and important ones, such as allergies, are also written on the kitchen board or job sheets. Staff add new things they notice. When the guest returns, the team can get everything ready without asking again. This makes the guest feel known and valued, so they are more likely to book again, tell their friends and write good reviews, which brings the villa more business.
markingPoints: Recorded promptly and clearly in the profile, with the date
Kept secure; only staff who need it can see it
Shared at briefings; key items such as allergies also written for the kitchen
Staff add new preferences they notice
Guests feel valued, so they return, recommend the villa and leave good reviews

practical1.title: Plan and set up a personalised arrival for a villa guest
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a made-up guest profile and booking, for example: Mr and Mrs Thompson, a repeat couple celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary, arriving at 3:00 p.m.; Mrs Thompson is allergic to shellfish; they like firm pillows, a cool room, Blue Mountain coffee and fresh mango; and they want the fridge stocked. As a group, plan the arrival: fill in a pre-arrival checklist, write a shopping list with prices in J$ within the budget the assessor gives, write an allergy note for the kitchen and a personal welcome note, and plan an anniversary touch. Then set up the Centre's mock villa bedroom and kitchen area: make the bed with the right pillows, set the room ready, place the welcome note and a local amenity, and put the (practice) groceries in the fridge and pantry. Each member is responsible for one part and explains it to the assessor. Finally, one member greets the "guests" (the assessor or members) by name, and the group updates the guest profile form. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and paperwork to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A made-up guest profile and booking (from the assessor)
Pre-arrival checklist, shopping list form, guest profile form and pens
The Centre's mock villa bedroom with bed linen and a choice of soft and firm pillows
Practice groceries or empty packets, and a fridge or a box marked "fridge"
Card and pens for the welcome note; a small local amenity (for example fruit or coffee)
A phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The completed pre-arrival checklist and shopping list
The allergy note for the kitchen
The bed made with the guests' choice of pillows
The welcome note and amenity in place
checklist: Read the profile and picked out every preference and need
Completed their part of the plan (checklist, shopping list, notes) correctly and neatly
Kept the shopping list within the budget, with prices in J$
Passed on the allergy clearly in writing to the kitchen
Set up their part of the villa to the guests' preferences
Wrote a warm, correct, personal welcome note
Greeted the guests by title and surname, warmly and confidently
safety: Lift mattresses and boxes with bent knees and a straight back; get help with heavy items
Use only made-up guest names and details
Keep any real food chilled and covered, and wash hands before handling it
Keep walkways clear of boxes and bags

practical2.title: Set up a private patio dinner and handle personal service requests (role play)
practical2.brief: As a group, set up a private dinner table for two on the Centre's patio or a training area, for a guest's special occasion given by the assessor (a birthday, a honeymoon or an anniversary). Set the table neatly with a cloth, napkins, cutlery, glasses and safe decoration (flowers, and candles only in glass holders, or battery candles), with a menu card that marks any allergy. Then each member in turn handles one personal service role play with a "guest" (another member or the assessor), for example: a pre-arrival phone call to find out preferences; an unpacking service; a guest who speaks little English; a guest who asks for something the villa cannot provide; a guest whose special request was forgotten; and a short feedback talk at the end of the stay. After each role play, the member writes the new preference or the action taken on the guest profile form. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and forms to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A table, two chairs, a tablecloth, napkins, cutlery, glasses and a small flower arrangement
Battery candles, or candles in glass holders
Card and pens for a menu card
A suitcase with practice clothes, hangers and a luggage rack (for the unpacking role play)
Guest profile forms and pens, and a phone or tablet to take the photos
photos: The table before it is set
The finished table set for two, with the menu card
Each member's role play in progress
The unpacking service: items hung and folded neatly
The area cleared and tidied at the end
checklist: Helped set a neat, safe and attractive table for the occasion
Greeted the guest politely and listened carefully
Found out the guest's needs or preferences with suitable questions
Handled their role play politely and correctly, offering a fair alternative where needed
Respected the guest's privacy and belongings
Recorded the preference or action clearly on the guest profile form
Helped clear and tidy the area
safety: Use battery candles, or keep real candles in glass holders away from cloth and flowers, and never leave them burning unattended
Carry glasses and cutlery on a tray; report and clear any broken glass safely
Lift the suitcase with bent knees onto the rack, not the bed
Use only made-up guest names and details
